item.title: Yamanashi Wine & Katsunuma: Japan's Birthplace of Wine — Guide
item.description: Yamanashi is the birthplace and heart of the Japanese wine industry, centred on the Katsunuma area near Kofu, where the mild climate and the native Koshu grape, a pale pink variety used to make crisp, delicate white wines, have supported winemaking since the 1870s. Today the region is home to dozens of wineries ranging from historic family operations to modern estates, many offering tastings, cellar tours and even hands-on blending experiences, set among vineyards that turn golden in autumn and often within walking or cycling distance of one another.
